generations.transcript: Welcome to your practice. Stand with your feet at a comfortable distance and let your shoulders soften. Inhale and feel the ribs widen. Exhale without forcing the breath. Let steadiness and ease share the work, and remember that you can change the shape at any time.

Scan from your feet toward your face and soften any effort the pose does not require.
Let your attention rest where the pose feels stable and clear.
Notice the places meeting the floor and let that contact make the pose more supported.

Feel the difference between useful muscular effort and gripping you can release.

Let your gaze be steady or your eyes close only if balance and comfort allow.

Let your breathing be the metronome, and let the pose adapt to it.
Notice the next inhale from its beginning to its end, then follow the exhale the same way.
Return attention to one uncomplicated breath in and one uncomplicated breath out.
Let the breath remain smooth and unforced; a smaller shape is always available.

Feel the ribs widen as you inhale and gently settle as you exhale.

If the breath becomes strained, ease the pose until breathing feels steady again.

Let the inhale create space and the exhale release effort you do not need.

Carry the steadiness of one conscious breath into whatever comes next.
Notice one quality from your practice that you would like to take beyond the mat.

Let steadiness and ease share the work.

Stay for another breath only if the pose remains clear and workable.
Welcome to your practice. Let comfort, steadiness, and an unforced breath guide you.

Feel the support beneath you and give yourself permission to take up space on your mat.

Allow the space between effort and ease to become a place of meditation.
Let the practice be an inquiry: what can be steady, and what can soften?
